name: Eune Mor
bio: Goose-herd of the North Fen, the fifth Mor to winter the grey geese at the fold. The geese come down from the clans' country in the first frost and she brings them in at dusk by singing, because a goose will follow a round it has heard since the egg. Since the singing under the carr stopped she has sat up every night on her deck singing the third voice, alone, so that somebody is.
unique_habit: Counts the geese in by knotting a withy cord as they pass the gate, a knot a goose and a red rush for a gander, and will not speak to anybody until the cord is done.

appearance.notes: a goose-feather tucked in the hood's band, a crook of withy worn smooth, knot-cords round both wrists

schedule.notes: letting the geese out onto the fen
the fold's withies mended where the hounds came through
singing the geese in, and then singing the third voice to the carr

name: Pello Mor
bio: Eune's grandson, nineteen, sent up from Moreva to learn the geese because nobody else in the family would. He cannot sing, and the geese know it, and follow him anyway, which Eune says is the worst sign she has ever seen in a goose-herd and the best.
unique_habit: Names every goose, including the ones his grandmother says must not be named because they will be eaten, and eats none of them.

appearance.notes: a leech-hound bite healing on the left forearm, a sling at the belt for the hounds, bare feet in the mud

schedule.notes: the water for the geese
mending the punt and watching the carr
the sling ready for the hounds

name: Aue Sa
bio: Apprentice to the last Keeper of the Unsung Vault, taken on at eleven because she could hold the second voice of the round under anybody's first. At the new moon the Keeper stopped singing and the lanterns began to go out, and Aue ran. She sleeps in the Old Crannog because nobody sleeps in it twice, and a girl who has broken the round should not sleep anywhere twice either; she lays the fire for the next one because that is what a Keeper does for whoever comes after.
unique_habit: Hums the second voice under whatever anybody says to her, very quietly, and stops, ashamed, whenever she notices.

appearance.notes: a Keeper's grey shawl too big for her, soot on the hands from the crannog's fire, a lantern-hook at the belt with no lantern on it

schedule.notes: in the crannog, on the stones, not on the bed
laying the fire for the next one
looking west toward the Vault

name: Tuo Lissa
bio: Keeper of Heron Watch, because the bittern that nests in its bell will not have anybody else near her, and she has had him for nine years. He writes each night on the bell-rope in knots, the way his grandmother taught him: what went up the channel, what came down, whether the lanterns burned out right. His grandmother went out under the Drowned Bell, and he has never missed a night's knot.
unique_habit: Answers questions in the bittern's time, which is to say after a long pause, all at once, and then not again.

appearance.notes: a bittern's barred feather pinned at the collar, the pale mark of the bell-rope across both palms, indigo-dyed sleeves rolled to the elbow

schedule.notes: the bittern is off her nest and he may come down
the day's knots, and the channel north
watching for boats with no lanterns

name: Hester Wrenn
bio: A Gosford woman who came down the Westway forty years ago behind a reedman selling eels, married him on Isse's Chair with a reed between them, and stayed when he went into the water twenty years later. She grows the only barley in Sedgemire on a patch of her island no bigger than a boat, and every Vale traveller the marsh has drowned since has come to her door first, she says, one way or another; she has made each of them a lantern, and hung it on the Long Jetty with their name on it.
unique_habit: Says 'in the Vale' before anything she disapproves of, and 'on the water' before anything she has come round to, and has been saying 'on the water' more every year.

appearance.notes: a Vale apron over reedfolk indigo, clay pipe, barley-chaff on the sleeves, a wedding reed plaited into a ring on the left hand

schedule.notes: weeding a barley patch the size of a boat
making lanterns, and naming them
sitting under the lanterns with her pipe

name: Wystan Crail
bio: Clerk to the Tallymen's Guild at the Eel Tally since the thaw, sent down from Lantern Row because he asked too many questions about a column there and somebody thought the marsh would cure him of it. It has not. He has found that his predecessor kept two books, and he intends to know why before the next boat goes up, and he is aware that the bravo on the steps is paid by the same people who paid his predecessor.
unique_habit: Counts everything under his breath, the herons, the eels, the planks of the steps, and loses count on purpose when anybody from the Delta is listening, to be polite.

appearance.notes: a Guild coat with the brass buttons turned green by the damp, ink to the second knuckle, wooden pattens strapped over good Tollmere shoes

schedule.notes: the barrels chalked, and the book
comparing the book with the barrels, again
reading the old clerk's second book

name: Maue Oul
bio: Tender of Isse's Chair, which means she ties every name said there on the naming-cord, clears the old reeds off the seat, and stands between the stilts for any couple who come to be married and cannot agree who should hold which end of the reed. She has tied eleven thousand knots and can read every one of them back, except the first, which she says is Isse's own.
unique_habit: Ties a knot in whatever is in her hands while she listens, and gives it to you when you go, and it is always your name, in a weave you did not tell her.

appearance.notes: a long indigo cord looped over one shoulder like a sash, rush-cuts on every finger, a reed behind each ear

schedule.notes: clearing the old reeds off the seat
tying the names

name: Illa Nauve
bio: The leech-wife of the east Delta: she keeps the black-backs and the striped leeches that Isseva's bleeders use, in sunken tubs under her stilt-house, and she bred the marsh hounds that were meant to keep the herons off them. The hounds learned from the leeches. At the thaw the old bitch slipped her collar and led them into the withies, and now they come back to the tubs every night, and not to the door.
unique_habit: Tests the weather by the leeches: if they climb the tub's side it will rain, if they lie still it will fog, and she has never once been wrong, and she is not proud of it.

appearance.notes: small round scars up both forearms, leather gauntlets to the elbow, a hound-whistle of bone on a cord

schedule.notes: with the door barred
the leeches fed and the tubs covered
selling leeches to whoever poles over from Isseva
at the collar pole, looking at the empty hook

name: Deo Oul
bio: Peat-cutter of the south marsh, third generation on the drying island. He cuts a thousand turves a week for Isseva's hearths and half of Tollmere's poorer streets, and is paid more for what he finds in the peat than for the peat, which he finds insulting and has stopped saying so.
unique_habit: Stacks the turves in the shape of loaves, the way his mother did, and will pull down a stack a stranger has built and build it again, politely.

appearance.notes: black to the elbows, a turf-spade with a blade worn to a crescent, a Builders' bronze pin he found and would not sell

schedule.notes: cutting
stacking, loaf by loaf

name: Lia Oul
bio: Deo's sister, who cuts beside him and keeps the finds-book, and who found the Warden. She talks to him in the evenings under his tarpaulin by the fire, because he was buried with a roll of names in his hand and a man who died holding names deserves to be talked to, and because, she says, he listens.
unique_habit: Brings every find to the fire and tells it where it is before she writes it down, in case it has been somewhere a long time and wants to know.

appearance.notes: a slate of finds on a cord, a small bronze bell she found, tied at the wrist where it does not ring

schedule.notes: cutting beside her brother
the finds-book, and the Warden under his tarpaulin
talking to the Warden
